skill.name: video-extend
skill.description: Extend or continue an existing video clip on RunComfy via the `runcomfy` CLI. Routes to Google Veo 3-1's `extend-video` and `fast/extend-video` endpoints — pick the source video plus a prompt describing what should happen next, and the model produces a clip that continues the original with consistent motion, lighting, and subject identity. Use when the user has a short Veo clip and wants it longer, or wants a chained narrative built shot-by-shot from a single seed clip. Triggers on "extend video", "continue video", "longer video", "video extend", "make this clip longer", "Veo extend", "chain video shots", "video continuation", or any explicit ask to take an existing video and add more frames after it.
skill.summary: Continue Veo 3.1 video clips through RunComfy with guided endpoint selection and continuation prompts.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: All 52 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, expected documentation links, a documented credential path, and unrelated phrase matches. However, the documented command embeds user-controlled URL and prompt values in single-quoted JSON without a shell-safe construction method, creating a plausible command-injection path. The workflow also transfers user media to RunComfy for external processing.

remediation.issue: User-controlled video URLs and prompts are shown inside a single-quoted shell argument without an escaping procedure.
remediation.suggestion: Construct the input with a structured serializer and pass it without shell interpolation. Document and test apostrophes, newlines, and shell metacharacters.

remediation.issue: The source video URL and continuation prompt are processed by an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the external transfer before execution and require user approval for sensitive, private, or access-controlled media.

content.value_statement: Short clips can end before a scene or narrative is complete. This skill continues Veo 3.1 clips through RunComfy with focused prompting guidance.
actual_capabilities: Selects standard or Fast Veo 3.1 Extend based on quality and cost priorities.
Continues an existing Veo clip from a user-provided video URL.
Creates focused continuation prompts for camera motion and one narrative beat.
Supports chained extensions by using each generated clip as the next input.
Downloads generated clips to a selected local output directory.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, authentication, and access to the Veo 3.1 endpoints.
Accepts an existing video URL and does not create the initial clip from a still image.
Identity drift can increase after several chained extensions.
Source video URLs and prompts are processed by RunComfy.

use_cases.title: Complete a Product Shot
use_cases.description: Continue a short product clip with a controlled camera move and one final action.

use_cases.title: Build a Narrative Sequence
use_cases.description: Chain several focused extensions to develop a scene one beat at a time.

use_cases.title: Draft Motion Variations
use_cases.description: Use Fast Extend for lower-cost iterations before generating the final continuation.

prompt_templates.title: Continue One Action
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this video from [video URL]. The subject completes [single action]. Keep the camera static and preserve the existing lighting.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs one simple continuation.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Camera Move
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue [video URL] as the camera [movement]. The subject [single action]. Preserve framing, identity, lighting, and background motion.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs controlled camera motion.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Cost Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend [video URL] with [scene beat]. Use Fast Extend for drafts and standard Extend for the final output in [directory].
prompt_templates.scenario: A team balances iteration cost and final quality.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Chained Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create [number] consecutive extensions from [video URL]. Define one action and one camera instruction per segment. Use each output as the next input.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user builds a longer narrative.

output_examples.input: Continue a studio product clip as the camera slowly moves closer and the display turns on.
output_examples.output: The standard Veo Extend route continues the camera movement, preserves the studio lighting, and adds the display activation as one beat.

output_examples.input: Draft a lower-cost continuation where the character turns toward the window.
output_examples.output: Fast Extend creates a draft continuation with the character turn, a stable camera, and consistent scene lighting.

output_examples.input: Create three connected story beats from the current clip.
output: Segment 2 uses the first result for one character action.
Segment 3 uses the second result for the closing beat.

best_practices: Describe only what happens next because the source clip already defines the scene.
Use one main action and one explicit camera instruction per extension.
Review every result before using it as input for another extension.
anti_patterns: Do not combine several unrelated actions in one continuation prompt.
Do not submit private media or signed URLs without approval for external processing.
Do not use long extension chains without checking identity and motion drift.

faq.question: What video models does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Google Veo 3.1 Extend or Veo 3.1 Fast Extend through RunComfy.

faq.question: Does it create a video from an image?
faq.answer: No. It continues an existing video clip from a supplied URL.

faq.question: When should I use Fast Extend?
faq.answer: Use Fast Extend for lower-cost drafts and early motion experiments.

faq.question: How should I write the continuation prompt?
faq.answer: Describe one next action and state the intended camera movement. Avoid repeating the full scene description.

faq.question: Can I chain several extensions?
faq.answer: Yes. Use each generated clip as the next input, then review for identity and motion drift.

faq.question: Where is the generated clip stored?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads the result to the output directory selected for the command.
